data.title: B2 Progress Check
data.description: A second mixed grammar and usage check to measure progress and confirm whether the learner is working securely at CEFR B2 level.

sections.sentence: Choose the correct sentence using a modal in the past.
sections.explain: Use 'should have' + past participle to describe something that would have been better to do in the past.

words.word: You should have told me about the problem earlier.
You should told me about the problem earlier.
You should have tell me about the problem earlier.

sections.sentence: Identify the correct sentence using the causative.
sections.explain: Use 'have' + object + past participle when someone else performs a service for you.

words.word: I had my car repaired last week.
I repaired my car by a mechanic last week.
I had repaired my car last week by a mechanic.

sections.sentence: Choose the correct sentence using an unreal past condition.
sections.explain: For an unreal past condition, use past perfect after 'if' and 'would have' + past participle in the result clause.

words.word: If they had left earlier, they wouldn't have missed the flight.
If they left earlier, they wouldn't have missed the flight.
If they had left earlier, they wouldn't miss the flight.

sections.sentence: Identify the correct reported speech structure.
sections.explain: When reporting a completed past action, the past simple often shifts to the past perfect.

words.word: He said that he had finished the report the day before.
He said that he has finished the report the day before.
He told that he had finished the report the day before.

sections.sentence: Choose the correct formal conditional structure.
sections.explain: 'Had I known...' is a formal alternative to 'If I had known...'.

words.word: Had I known about the delay, I would have taken a different train.
Had I knew about the delay, I would have taken a different train.
Had I known about the delay, I had taken a different train.

sections.sentence: Identify the correct non-defining relative clause.
sections.explain: Non-defining relative clauses use commas and usually 'who' or 'which', not 'that'.

words.word: My brother, who lives in Canada, is coming to visit.
My brother, that lives in Canada, is coming to visit.
My brother who he lives in Canada, is coming to visit.

sections.sentence: Choose the correct sentence with a linking expression.
sections.explain: 'Although' is followed by a clause, while 'despite' is followed by a noun or -ing form.

words.word: Although the journey was long, we enjoyed it.
Despite the journey was long, we enjoyed it.
Although of the long journey, we enjoyed it.

sections.sentence: Identify the correct verb pattern showing a change in meaning.
sections.explain: 'Remember to do' means not to forget a future action. 'Remember doing' refers to a memory of a past action.

words.word: Remember to lock the door before you leave.
Remember locking the door before you leave.
Remember lock the door before you leave.

sections.sentence: Choose the correct sentence using the future continuous.
sections.explain: Use 'will be' + verb-ing for an action that will be in progress at a particular future time.

words.word: This time tomorrow, I'll be flying to Madrid.
This time tomorrow, I'll fly to Madrid.
This time tomorrow, I'll be fly to Madrid.

sections.sentence: Identify the correct advanced comparison structure.
sections.explain: Use 'the + comparative, the + comparative' to show that two changes are connected.

words.word: The more you practise, the more confident you become.
The more you practise, more confident you become.
More you practise, the more confident you become.
